title: Pork Caldereta
description: A rich Filipino stew known for its tender meat and savory, slightly spicy tomato-based sauce thickened with liver spread.

ingredients.item: Pork shoulder, belly, or ribs, cut into 2-inch cubes

method.instruction: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic and onion until fragrant and the onion is translucent.
Add the pork cubes. Cook for about 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the meat is lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in the tomato sauce and water or broth. Add the bouillon cube. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and cover. Simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, or until the pork is fork-tender.
Stir in the liver spread until fully incorporated. If using chili peppers, add them now.
Add the potatoes and carrots. Cover and cook for about 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the bell peppers and olives. Cook for another 3 to 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving dish. If desired, top with shredded cheddar cheese while hot so it melts into the sauce.

notes.title: Crispy Vegetables
notes.content: To prevent the potatoes and carrots from going mushy, pan-fry them separately before adding to the stew at the end.

notes.title: Creamier Version
notes.content: Adding a tablespoon of peanut butter or a splash of coconut milk creates a richer, more modern take on this dish.

notes.title: Meat Choice
notes.content: Pork shoulder gives the best balance of tenderness and fat. Ribs add extra flavour but take longer to become fork-tender.

notes.title: Leftovers
notes.content: Caldereta keeps well refrigerated for up to 3 days and the flavour deepens overnight. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
